analysis: Reviewed scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (head, full file in two units). The PR changes only an offline CI workflow-structure unit test: it adds PROVIDER_SHARDS=[1,2,3,4,5] (line 81), asserts a per-shard matrix with fail-fast: false and per-shard route lanes (lines 199-219), and adds test_route_requests_exactly_one_lane_per_provider_shard (lines 227-233). It does not touch provider runtime code, coordinator contract, keys, attestation, App Attest, prefix-cache storage (T-041), the fan helper, or add-on sockets. Security-relevant behavior is limited to CI integrity: the test pins checkout and artifact action SHAs, asserts no continue-on-error, no secrets.* and no backend credentials in the provider job (line 721-722), and that Provider Tests gate requires all lanes. These assertions are strengthened or preserved, not weakened. The test spawns subprocesses with stub scripts in temp dirs and passes only fixture env; there is no injection from untrusted input. No new attack surface, no invalidated threat assumptions. Remaining unverified: the actual .github/workflows/ci.yml (route job, matrix, provider-test-gate) is outside the supplied units, so whether the workflow matches these assertions is not verified here. That is a CI correctness question rather than a demonstrated security regression.
